Topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Race of Curves

Target audience: University students (Physics/Engineering/Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Challenge of Descent

Lecture lines:
Can we reach the bottom faster?
Not by taking a straight path.
Compare straight line and curve.
A secret path hides beneath.
This is the Brachistochrone problem.

Planned animations:
Create title text "Introduction: The Challenge of Descent" in #FFFFFF.
Fade in two beads at different points on a curve.
Show beads sliding down to illustrate time comparison.
Highlight the curve path with #FF00FF color.
Fade out beads and curve to end section.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Intuition: Energy and Velocity

Lecture lines:
Energy dictates speed, gravity drives descent.
Gaining velocity early is crucial.
Curvature helps build speed quickly.

Planned animations:
Create title text "Prerequisite Intuition: Energy and Velocity" in #FFFFFF.
Display kinetic energy formula K = 0.5 * m * v^2 in #00FFFF.
Animate energy bar filling up as velocity increases.
Flash the velocity term in the formula.
Fade out formula and bar to end section.

Section: section_3 — The Mathematical Reveal: The Cycloid

Lecture lines:
The solution is a Cycloid.
A point on a rolling circle.
It traces a path of wonder.
Mathematics defines this elegant arc.
Optimal descent meets perfect geometry.

Planned animations:
Create title text "The Mathematical Reveal: The Cycloid" in #FFFFFF.
Draw a cycloid path using MathTex equation.
Label the cycloid with #FFFF00 text.
Trace the cycloid curve with a bright #FFFFFF point.
Fade out to end section.

Section: section_4 — Verification: Why Cycloid Wins

Lecture lines:
Straight lines are short but slow.
Cycloids sacrifice distance for velocity.
Watch the race, see reality.

Planned animations:
Create title text "Verification: Why Cycloid Wins" in #FFFFFF.
Show comparative graph of descent times.
Label shortest path line in #00FF00.
Fade out comparison to end section.

Section: section_5 — Real-World Application & Summary

Lecture lines:
This birthed the calculus of variations.
Nature uses paths to optimize time.
From rollercoasters to diving eagles.

Planned animations:
Create title text "Real-World Application & Summary" in #FFFFFF.
Animate real-world object using cycloidal path.
Fade out object and title to end section.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Can we reach the bottom faster?",
            "Not by taking a straight path.",
            "Compare straight line and curve.",
            "A secret path hides beneath.",
            "This is the Brachistochrone problem."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Challenge of Descent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements

        B = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        straight_path = Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*2 + RIGHT*2)
        curve_path = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t*2, -1.5*np.sin(t*np.pi), 0]), t_range=[0, 1])

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "This birthed the calculus of variations.", 
            "Nature uses paths to optimize time.", 
            "From rollercoasters to diving eagles."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Cycloid Path Trajectory for an "eagle" icon
        # Parametric: x = r(t - sin(t)), y = -r(1 - cos(t))
        r = 0.5
        def cycloid(t):
            return np.array([r * (t - np.sin(t)), -r * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])
        
        path = ParametricFunction(cycloid, t_range=[0, 2*PI], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(path, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        eagle = Dot(color=RED).move_to(path.get_start())
        self.add(path, eagle)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(eagle, path), run_time=3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(path), FadeOut(eagle))
